correctness.rationale: Reconstructed orthonormal basis 1, x_i/sqrt(s), (x_i²−s)/sqrt(h), x_i x_j/s, hence exact full degree≤2 reproducing kernel with cross-chaos (B²−D)/(2s²). Linear and diagonal terms have uniform L² size O(sqrt(d)); the cross term has O(d) size. For any triangular evaluation array with q_d→q>0, bounded Lindeberg sums imply B/sqrt(d)⇒sqrt(sq)Z, and D/d→sq in L². Cross term divided by d⇒(q/(2s))(Z²−1), uniformly integrable from exact chaos orthogonality L² bound q_d²/(2s²). At q=0 the same bound proves zero limit. Compactness of q_d in [0,1] upgrades all sequential limits to uniform spatial convergence. E|Z²−1|=4/sqrt(2*pi*e), so coefficient 2q/(s sqrt(2*pi*e)). Endpoint ±1 in support gives norm extremum asymptotically; q_d→1 iff average deficit→0; no finite exact-max claim.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS: Trefethen’s full seven-page analytic polynomial-approximation paper concerns convergence versus polynomial degree and Euclidean degree; the continuous total-degree-two projector endpoint norm as dimension tends to infinity is not its theorem. Published Johnson/Hamming quadratic idempotent norms share the centered chi-square Gaussian constant, but their finite association-scheme domains and projectors are mathematically distinct; they neither handle arbitrary continuous symmetric marginals nor the diagonal-quadratic terms and uniform spatial corner profile. Discrete three-dimensional cube hyperinterpolation is also different. Potential general polynomial-chaos results remain a residual risk.
